title: Polynomial value and differential equations on the singular fibre
statement: Let k be a field, f:Y -> Spec k smooth, L invertible, and s_i any finite family of sections, indexed by a type I in the scheme universe. Use the universal family and its reduced singular scheme [def-zl-bertini-universal-family]. Fix an open U in Y and z in U, K=kappa_U(z), an open W containing U.ι(z), and any free generator e of L on W [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Let a_i be the actual coefficient of s_i|W in e. There are a commutative K-algebra A, an isomorphism of the singular fibre over z with Spec A, and a surjective K-algebra map q:K[x_i] -> A. For every K-linear functional phi on K plus the actual relative cotangent fibre at z, q(sum_i phi(a_i(z),da_i(z))*x_i)=0, using the jets defined in [lem-zl-bertini-local-first-jets]. The isomorphism followed by the coefficient Spec map with variables q(x_i) and scalars k -> K -> A equals the original coefficient projection of this singular fibre. Fibres are scheme-theoretic [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There is no generation, immersion, affine-open, or jet-rank hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0FD6, lemma-bertini, final paragraph; supplemented by Morphisms Tag 02G1 and Algebra Tag 00T7

proof.text: Use the canonical polynomial coordinate map of the actual singular fibre. It is a closed immersion, hence its source T is affine. Take A=Gamma(T,O_T), the specified K-algebra structure rho composed with C, j=T.isoSpec, and q the actual rho as an algebra homomorphism. Its surjectivity is already proved.

Apply the first-jet tensor vanishing theorem. For any K-linear functional phi, apply TensorProduct.map(id,phi) followed by TensorProduct.rid. Its value on q(x_i) tensor jet_i is phi(jet_i) times q(x_i). Map the finite sum and use q(C a)=algebraMap a to obtain the asserted polynomial equation.

Rewrite MvPolynomial.map as eval2Hom and use MvPolynomial.comp_eval₂Hom. The resulting scalar homomorphism is definitionally the chosen K-algebra map composed with k -> K, and the variable images are definitionally q(X i). Naturality of toSpecGamma reconstructs the canonical coordinate map from rho. Its first projection identity is precisely the original coefficient morphism, proving the displayed equality.

lean.statement:
theorem bertini_singular_fibre_polynomial_equations
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth f]
    (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    {I : Type u} [Fintype I] (s : I → Γ(L, ⊤))
    (U : Y.Opens) (z : U) (W : Y.Opens) (hz : U.ι z ∈ W)
    (e : Γ(L, W)) (he : Scheme.Modules.IsFreeGenerator e) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : Algebra ((U : Scheme).residueField z) A),
      ∃ (j : (bertiniSingularToSource f L s ∣_ U).fiber z ≅ Spec (.of A))
        (q : MvPolynomial I ((U : Scheme).residueField z) →ₐ[
          (U : Scheme).residueField z] A),
        Function.Surjective q ∧
        (∀ φ : Module.Dual ((U : Scheme).residueField z)
            ((U : Scheme).residueField z × bertiniCotangentFibre f U z),
          q (∑ i, MvPolynomial.C (φ (bertiniLocalFirstJet f U z W hz
            (he.coeff (L.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : W ≤ ⊤)).op (s i))))) *
            MvPolynomial.X i) = 0) ∧
        j.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom
          ((algebraMap ((U : Scheme).residueField z) A).comp
            ((U.ι ≫ f).residueFieldAlgebraMap z))
          (fun i ↦ q (MvPolynomial.X i)))) =
            (bertiniSingularToSource f L s ∣_ U).fiberι z ≫
              ((bertiniSingularToSource f L s) ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫
              (bertiniSingularIdeal f L s).subschemeι ≫ bertiniUniversalProjection f L s
